item.title: OpenRLHF 0.10 Adds Multi-Turn VLM RLHF with FlashREINFORCE Support
item.description:
OpenRLHF 0.10 Adds Multi-Turn VLM RLHF with FlashREINFORCE Support

OpenRLHF 0.10 introduces Multi-Turn Vision-Language Model (VLM) Reinforcement Learning and VLM RLHF support, enabling end-to-end training of models like Qwen3.5 with image inputs. The framework also adds FlashREINFORCE, a critic-free, single-rollout asynchronous RL approach for agentic language models. Additional improvements include ProRL V2 integration for prolonged training and the MARTI fork for multi-agent system training.

item.title: Agency Swarm Updates Framework with OpenAI Agents SDK Integration and 2.0 Beta
item.description:
Agency Swarm Updates Framework with OpenAI Agents SDK Integration and 2.0 Beta

Agency Swarm has updated to a new SDK-based version, including a 2.0 beta release, designed for building, orchestrating, and managing multi-agent applications. The framework leverages and extends the OpenAI Agents SDK to simplify creating AI agencies, continuing the original vision of Arsenii Shatokhin (aka VRSEN) to structure automation around real-world organizational concepts.

🔍 Overview

Agency Swarm provides a structured orchestration layer on top of the OpenAI Agents SDK. Built with a production-ready focus, the framework emphasizes reliability and deployment in real-world environments. It targets the OpenAI Agents SDK and the Responses API.

🧩 Key Features

  • Customizable Agent Roles: Define distinct roles such as CEO, Virtual Assistant, or Developer with tailored instructions, tools, and capabilities.
  • Full Prompt Control: Maintain complete control over each agent’s guiding instructions.
  • Type-Safe Tools: Develop tools using Pydantic models for automatic argument validation compatible with the OpenAI Agents SDK FunctionTool format. Tools can be created using the @function_tool decorator, extending BaseTool, or importing OpenAPI schemas via ToolFactory.from_openapi_schema().
  • Orchestrated Communication: Agents communicate using a dedicated send_message tool, with interactions controlled by explicit directional communication_flows defined on the Agency.
  • State Persistence: Persist conversation history across database or file storage using load_threads_callback and save_threads_callback.

⚙️ Technical Specifications

  • Python Support: Python 3.12+
  • Operating Systems: macOS, Linux, Windows
  • Default Model: gpt-6-luna (served by the Responses API)
  • LiteLLM Router Integrations: Anthropic (Claude), Google (Gemini), Grok (xAI), Azure OpenAI, and OpenRouter (gateway)

🚀 Getting Started and Migration

To install the framework, use pip install -U agency-swarm. To try the 2.0 beta, install using pip install -U --pre agency-swarm. Projects transitioning from v0.x or upgrading to v2 can consult the respective Migration Guide and v2 migration notes.

Setup requires an OPENAI_API_KEY defined in an auto-loaded .env file or exported in the shell environment. It is recommended to begin project development using the Agency Starter Template.

#AgencySwarm #OpenAI #AIAgents #Python #MultiAgent

Source: VRSEN/agency-swarm

item.title: Swarms-rs: First Enterprise-Grade Multi-Agent Orchestration Framework in Rust
item.description:
Swarms-rs: First Enterprise-Grade Multi-Agent Orchestration Framework in Rust

Swarms-rs has launched as the first-ever enterprise-grade, production-ready multi-agent orchestration framework built in Rust. The framework is designed to handle demanding tasks with unparalleled speed and efficiency, leveraging Rust’s performance and safety features to provide a scalable solution for multi-agent systems.

🔍 Overview

An agent in Swarms-rs is defined as an entity powered by an LLM equipped with tools and memory that can run autonomously to automate issues. The framework seamlessly manages and coordinates thousands of agents, allowing them to communicate and collaborate efficiently to achieve complex goals.

⚙️ Key Details

Key features and capabilities include:

  • Built with Rust’s zero-cost abstractions and fearless concurrency for optimal resource use
  • Near-zero latency and lightning-fast execution, ideal for high-frequency and real-time applications
  • Memory safety guaranteed through Rust’s ownership model, eliminating data races and memory leaks
  • Minimal overhead with maximum throughput and efficiency
  • Highly modular design for easy extension and customization
  • Scales from a handful of agents to millions while maintaining top-tier performance
  • Designed for real-world deployment with robustness for mission-critical tasks

💻 Technical Requirements

To use Swarms-rs, the following are required:

Requirement Description
Rust (latest stable version recommended) Programming language runtime
Cargo package manager Rust’s package manager
LLM API key For OpenAI, DeepSeek, Anthropic, etc.
Dependencies Multiple crates including tokio, anyhow, dotenv, and others

🚀 Availability

Installation is straightforward:

  • Run cargo add swarms-rs
  • Add supporting packages: cargo add tokio --features full, cargo add anyhow dotenv, and others
  • Create a .env file in your project root with API credentials

📊 Why It Matters

Swarms-rs represents a significant advancement in multi-agent system orchestration, offering developers a robust, efficient, and scalable solution built on Rust’s proven track record of performance and safety. The framework’s ability to handle mission-critical tasks while maintaining efficiency under heavy loads makes it an attractive option for industries requiring reliable, high-performance agent-based systems.

#Rust #MultiAgent #Orchestration #LLM #Enterprise

Source: The-Swarm-Corporation/swarms-rs

item.title: gym-pybullet-drones refactored for gymnasium and Betaflight SITL
item.description:
gym-pybullet-drones refactored for gymnasium and Betaflight SITL

A minimalist refactoring of the gym-pybullet-drones repository has been released to ensure compatibility with gymnasium, stable-baselines3 2.0, and betaflight SIM. The project, originally featured in GitHub’s Maintainer Spotlight 2026, now supports both single-agent and multi-agent tasks with updated system requirements.

🔍 Overview

  • Refactoring Goal: Minimalist update for compatibility with gymnasium, stable-baselines3 2.0, and betaflight SITL.
  • Version Control: The original IROS 2021 codebase is accessible via git checkout [paper|master].
  • Citation: Users are encouraged to cite the IROS 2021 paper and the original codebase.

🧩 How it works

  • Single-Agent Task: One drone hovers at z == 1.0.
  • Multi-Agent Task: Two drones hover at z == 1.2 and 0.7 respectively.
  • PettingZooWrapper: Exposes multi-drone aviary through PettingZoo’s Parallel API, assigning one agent per drone (drone_0, drone_1, …).
  • Observation and Reward: Each agent receives its own row of the aviary’s observation. The aviary’s team reward and episode flags are shared by all agents.
  • Centralized Critics: env.state() returns every drone’s kinematics for centralized critics.

⚙️ Key details

Requirement Details
Operating Systems Tested on Intel x64/Ubuntu 24.04 and Apple Silicon/macOS 26
Python & pybullet Requires Python 3.10+; pybullet has no pre-built wheel for versions beyond 3.10
Ubuntu Setup Install gcc to allow pip3 install to build pybullet
SITL Setup One-time setup requires building one SITL executable per drone from the repo’s top folder
Dependencies --num_drones must be less than or equal to the number passed to clone_bfs.sh; curl may be required via apt install

💡 Why it matters

The PettingZooWrapper makes the environment usable with Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) libraries built on PettingZoo. The refactoring ensures the environment remains functional with modern reinforcement learning stacks like stable-baselines3 2.0 while supporting Betaflight SITL for drone simulation.

#gym-pybullet-drones #ReinforcementLearning #Multi-Agent #gymnasium #betaflight

Source: learnsyslab/gym-pybullet-drones

item.title: AWS Quick Updates Enable Deterministic Multi-Agent Workflows and Desktop Integration
item.description:
AWS Quick Updates Enable Deterministic Multi-Agent Workflows and Desktop Integration

AWS has released updates to AWS Quick, an AI workspace built specifically for work. These updates are designed to help teams complete everyday tasks by allowing users to describe a process in chat, which Quick then builds into a flow that orchestrates agents, skills, and tools with access to structured data, knowledge, and apps.

🧩 How it works

Users can now build, run, and refine flows entirely in chat. The system introduces new deterministic steps to make workflows consistent and verifiable, supporting longer-running processes and large data volumes. With multi-agent orchestration, several specialized agents work on a request simultaneously, and Quick combines their findings into a single response.

Example Workflow: Financial Reporting

The update demonstrates a workflow for Maya, a financial planning and analysis manager, who prepares monthly reports for her VP of Finance. Previously, this process lived in her memory and a personal checklist, meaning teammates had to rebuild the report from scratch when she was out. Quick builds the flow from her description, allowing her to test and refine it in the same conversation. A diagram beside the chat displays each step for verification. The flow performs the following actions:

  • Pulls last month’s results from the team’s monthly results dashboard in Quick.
  • Compares each region to the annual plan in a budget spreadsheet using set formulas to ensure consistent calculations.
  • Flags regions that moved significantly from plan based on user-set thresholds and drafts commentary using a team-specific skill.
  • Drafts a Microsoft Excel summary to a shared Space and report email, and notifies the team in Slack that the draft is ready.

Jordan, an analyst on Maya’s team, can run this flow from the Quick desktop app. The flow can utilize local resources, such as a spreadsheet of regional adjustments saved on his computer. Before the report is finalized, Jordan reviews the draft, asks for changes in chat, and approves it for the VP of Finance.

⚙️ Key details

The updated web app places items needing attention and a daily briefing on the home screen, adds agents and skills used on desktop, and keeps work running after the tab is closed. Quick also supports connections to external tools like Meta ads and Amplitude, allowing users to ask questions in natural language and combine answers with other sources. Language support has expanded to include Japanese, German, Chinese (Simplified and Traditional), and Vietnamese.

💡 Why it matters

AWS Quick Flows helps teams automate and standardize business processes. For organizations, this allows data teams to focus on complex, high-impact work. One retailer reported that without growing its team, nearly four times as many people now work with data each month. A single use case already saves 80 hours of work per month, shifting the culture from a few people building solutions to an organization where everyone can create, experiment, and change how they work.

#AWS #AIagents #WorkflowAutomation #Productivity #MultiAgent

Source: New in AWS Quick: More capable flows, an updated web experience, and agents that work together | Amazon Web Services

item.title: PenShot multi-agent system converts scripts to video generation prompts
item.description:
PenShot multi-agent system converts scripts to video generation prompts

A new open-source system called PenShot uses a multi-agent LangGraph pipeline to parse scripts of any format and generate coherent, model-ready prompts for text-to-video models including Sora, Veo, Runway, Kling, and SVD.

🔍 Overview

PenShot (剧本分镜智能体) is a script-to-storyboard agent that takes input from movies, anime, short dramas, or novels and produces shot-level descriptions and video generation prompts. It is built on LLMs orchestrated through LangGraph and LlamaIndex, with a focus on maintaining character, scene, and plot consistency across segments.

🧩 How it works

The system operates as a directed multi-agent graph:

  • Script parsing agent → Storyboard generation agent
  • Storyboard generation agent → Video segmentation agent
  • Video segmentation agent → Prompt conversion agent
  • Prompt conversion agent → Quality audit agent
  • Quality audit agent → Continuity guard agent
  • Continuity guard agent → Auxiliary generation agent (three-view/background/keyframe)
  • Multi-model adapter → Sora / Veo / Runway / 可灵 / SVD
  • Sora / Veo / Runway / 可灵 / SVD → FFmpeg synthesis
  • FFmpeg synthesis → Final film

Continuity is enforced through a three-view design, a RAG knowledge base, three-tier memory (short/medium/long term), Chroma vector retrieval, snapshot mechanism, and multi-dimensional recall. A task-pool priority queue manages execution order.

⚙️ Key details

Supported input and output

  • Accepts arbitrary-format scripts: movies, short dramas, anime, novels
  • Auto-identifies scenes, dialogue, and action instructions
  • Understands story structure and supports long-text segmented processing
  • Outputs shot-granularity segments with precise duration planning adapted to each video model’s length limits

Prompt generation

  • Bilingual (Chinese/English) visual descriptions
  • Negative prompts
  • Audio prompts
  • Ready-to-use for Sora, Veo, Runway, Kling (可灵), SVD

Model and LLM compatibility

Component Options
Text-to-video models Sora, Veo, Runway, 可灵, SVD
LLM providers OpenAI, Qwen, DeepSeek, Ollama (pluggable)

Integration interfaces

  • Python SDK
  • REST API
  • LangGraph nodes
  • Function Calling
  • MCP (Model Context Protocol) standard interface
  • A2A collaboration protocol

Reliability features

  • Automatic retry and error fallback
  • Bidirectional traceability: every storyboard segment links back to its source script position

🚀 Availability

  • Package install: pip install penshot (3 lines of code to integrate)
  • Docker: docker pull neotems/penshot to run as a service
  • Claimed 5-minute onboarding

💡 Why it matters

PenShot addresses the gap between narrative scripts and the strict prompt requirements of current text-to-video models. By combining multi-agent orchestration, persistent memory, vector retrieval, and multi-model adapter layers, it provides an end-to-end pipeline that preserves narrative continuity while outputting prompts tailored to each target video generator.

#AIagents #LangGraph #TextToVideo #ScriptToVideo #MultiAgent #OpenSource

Source: neopen/story-shot-agent

item.title: AWS Announces Pluggable Agentic AI Framework for Production‑Scale Multi‑Agent Applications
item.description:
AWS Announces Pluggable Agentic AI Framework for Production‑Scale Multi‑Agent Applications

The Pluggable Agentic AI Framework is a new reference architecture that guides organizations in moving multi‑agent AI applications from prototype to production scale.

🧩 Overview

  • A seven‑layer composable reference architecture for multi‑agent AI.
  • Each layer has a distinct responsibility and a stable contract.
  • The services shown are examples; alternatives can be substituted to match existing infrastructure.
  • The architecture provides a blueprint for building, securing, and operating agentic AI at production scale.

📚 Data & Knowledge Layer

  • Foundation of Agentic AI; an agent is only as good as the data it can access.
  • Owns retrieval, embeddings, and access to structured and unstructured data through a clear contract: accept a query and return the most relevant information for context.
  • Example building blocks (reference implementation):
Component Role
Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Base Stores and serves knowledge for agents
Vector Engine for Amazon OpenSearch Serverless Provides vector search capabilities
Amazon S3 Vectors Persists vector representations
Amazon DynamoDB Offers fast key‑value access

⚙️ Model & Inference Routing Layer

  • Model choices are driven by configuration, not hard‑wired logic.
  • Use smaller, faster models for simple tasks; larger models for nuanced reasoning.
  • A model routing layer keeps agents decoupled from hosting environments and provider‑specific APIs via a consistent request‑and‑response contract.
  • A proxy such as LiteLLM offers a common interface across providers, enabling model swaps without rewriting application code.

🎯 Orchestration Layer

  • Determines how work is distributed.
  • Simple tasks: a single agent handles end‑to‑end work.
  • Complex, cross‑domain workflows: a supervisor delegates to specialist agents, each scoped to a specific capability and toolset.
  • Benefits of splitting responsibilities:
    • Keeps each agent’s context focused.
    • Makes latency more predictable.
    • Allows independent testing, scaling, and security modeling.
  • Enforce bounded autonomy: specialists execute only within granted tools.
  • Supervisor discovers specialists via a centralized agent registry and invokes them through standard protocols like MCP (Model Context Protocol) and A2A (Agent to Agent).
  • Example components: Strands Agents for specialists, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore harness for orchestrator, AWS Agent Registry and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway for discovery and routing.

🔐 Security & Guardrails Layer

  • Treated as a primary concern from day one.
  • All external content is considered untrusted by default.
  • Every request—whether from a user, another agent, or an automated workflow—is authenticated, e.g., via Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity.
  • Fine‑grained access control determines whether a tool call is permitted before execution.
  • Agents receive temporary, scoped credentials rather than persistent secrets.

🔄 Flexibility & Substitution

  • While the reference implementation uses specific AWS services, organizations may replace any layer with alternatives that align with their existing infrastructure and requirements.
  • The stable contracts between layers ensure that substitutions do not break the overall system.

#AWS #AgenticAI #MultiAgent #Architecture

Source: Pluggable Agentic AI Framework: A seven-layer composable enterprise agentic AI reference architecture on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore | Amazon Web Services

item.title: TandemBench Introduces Benchmark for Multi-Agent Decision Models
item.description:
TandemBench Introduces Benchmark for Multi-Agent Decision Models

On 4 Nov 2026, a paper titled TandemBench: Benchmarking Decision Models for Multi‑Agent Collaboration was submitted to the Computer Science > Computation and Language category. The work presents a new benchmark designed to evaluate how decision models handle coordination in multi‑agent settings.

🔍 Overview

  • Decision models pick among predefined options in tasks such as routing and action selection.
  • In multi‑agent collaboration, a decision determines how members divide work, exchange resources, and act in parallel.

🍳 Benchmark Details

  • TandemBench contains 1,200 questions based on multi‑agent cooking scenarios where coordination choices affect goal completion.
  • Models are given:
    1. Complete global information,
    2. A set of candidate team plans.
  • Reference answers are generated through execution and exact search.
  • Two evaluation modes are used:
    • Selecting the optimal team plan.
    • In paired variants (retain or remove the optimal plan), judging whether better arrangements exist beyond the supplied options.

📊 Evaluation Results

Model Type Count
Native decision models 40
General‑purpose language models 10
  • The best native decision model achieved 62.50 % decision accuracy.
  • Native decision models performed close to chance when verifying optimality.
  • Paired tests showed that some models reported better alternatives regardless of whether an optimal plan was already present.
  • The findings indicate that high decision‑accuracy alone can mask systematic errors in judging the optimality of supplied options.

🚀 Availability

  • The dataset and evaluation code are publicly available at the provided HTTPS URL.

💡 Why it matters

  • Provides a concrete, large‑scale testbed for assessing coordination capabilities of AI decision systems.
  • Highlights a gap between selecting the best plan and correctly evaluating the optimality of available options, guiding future model development.

#AI #MultiAgent #DecisionModels #Benchmark

Source: TandemBench: Benchmarking Decision Models for Multi-Agent Collaboration

item.title: Ripwire: Zero‑Dependency C++23 CLI for Multi‑Agent Code Navigation
item.description:
Ripwire: Zero‑Dependency C++23 CLI for Multi‑Agent Code Navigation

The new tool ripwire provides a zero‑dependency C++23 CLI + MCP server for coding agents.

🔍 Overview

  • “Zero‑dependency C++23 CLI + MCP server for coding agents.”
  • “Find what you want without reading the repo, then check you built what you meant — blast radius, tests-to-run, quality deltas.”
  • “Signatures at 74.7% fewer bytes than bodies; every guess labelled, every loss published.”
  • “Ranked, deterministic call graph: what to touch, what it breaks, which tests to run.”
  • “On the edit: blast radius, tests that reach it, eleven quality kinds reporting only what got worse, forgotten co‑changes, fields read and written, names that resolve more than one way.”

🧩 How it works

  • The tool builds a deterministic call graph that tells you what to touch, what it breaks, and which tests to run.
  • It reports blast radius and the set of tests that reach any edit.
  • Signatures are stored at 74.7% fewer bytes than full bodies, with every guess labelled and every loss published.
  • Queries such as --callers and --edit-check surface hidden dependencies and incompatibilities that plain text search would miss.

⚙️ Key details

  • “Whole‑workflow ~2×; per‑lookup 10–25×; and two moments where one call was worth more than the rest of the session’s tooling combined.”
  • “Roughly half the total token spend of the audit/research phase, saved.”
  • “A single doc‑recall call served the relevant sections of a 164KB planning document in ~6K tokens (~25×).”
  • “Agents that led with the tool ran ~30–40% leaner on tool‑call counts than agents doing raw read fan‑outs over comparable questions.”
  • “Two tasks had their direction changed by a single call.”
  • “One --callers query returned zero production callers, redirecting the task to the real gap.”
  • “--edit-check flagged 5 of 6 call sites as incompatible — sites a text search had missed — that would otherwise have silently diverged from the canonical path …”
  • “A dozen‑plus real code‑quality defects fixed, not waived, across ~15 implementing agents — all caught by --quality-delta at each agent’s "I think I’m done" moment.”
  • “Examples include a 480‑token duplicated routine, a fourth private copy of a shared RNG utility, a hand‑duplicated cost function, a pair of near‑identical functions with a flipped sign, test‑fixture duplication across sibling suites, and functions that had quietly absorbed a second job.”
  • “None of these would have failed a test; all of them are the sediment that rots a codebase under high‑velocity multi‑agent development.”
  • “The gate made removing them routine instead of heroic.”

🚀 Availability

  • “Just want to use it? Install it with the one line below, then start each coding session by telling your agent to use it, for example: "Use ripwire on this repo."”
  • “The install also teaches your agent when to reach for each command.”
  • “Want every detail? The reference guide near the bottom covers install, commands, output format, exit codes and limits.”
  • “You do not need it to get started.”

💡 Why it matters

  • For a single developer, the tool is a “good lookup accelerator.”
  • For an orchestrated fleet, it is “load‑bearing: it halved the research spend, twice redirected tasks before wasted work, prevented at least one silent‑divergence shipped bug, and turned code‑quality hygiene from a hope into a per‑task mechanical gate.”
  • The reported field study was written by Claude Fable 5.0, the frontier model orchestrating ~20 coding agents over two days on a ~1,500‑file C++/Metal codebase.

#AIcoding #Ripwire #CodeQuality #MultiAgent

Source: redhat-et/ripwire

item.title: 2025 Marks Shift to Autonomous Multi‑Agent AI Systems
item.description:
2025 Marks Shift to Autonomous Multi‑Agent AI Systems

In 2025 the AI landscape moved from passive prompt‑response models to autonomous agents that can plan, code, and validate work without constant human direction.

🔍 Overview

  • Earlier language models waited for explicit human instruction at every computational step.
  • Modern autonomous AI trends establish continuous‑operation paradigms where systems evaluate high‑level objectives, generate internal sub‑goals, and execute complex workflows without constant human oversight.
  • The human role changes from typist to director.

🧩 How it works

  • Agent architecture maintains state and uses scratchpads for intermediate reasoning, looping until validation criteria pass.
  • Probabilistic reasoning engines evaluate environment states, select optimal tools, and modify execution paths dynamically.
  • When data is missing or errors occur, the system queries internal memory, tests alternative APIs, or restructures the execution tree autonomously.
  • Multi‑agent collaboration divides massive operational workloads into manageable micro‑tasks.
Agent Type Role
Planner Evaluates high‑level objectives and creates internal sub‑goals
Coder Generates code to implement the sub‑goals
QA Reviewer Validates output against criteria and provides feedback
  • Frameworks such as LangGraph and AutoGen orchestrate communication protocols between instances.

⚙️ Key details

  • Traditional software runs deterministic branching logic; autonomous systems use probabilistic reasoning and dynamic tool selection.
  • Heavy models run in centralized cloud data centers incur high latency and compute cost.
  • Hardware manufacturers now ship specialized NPUs to consumer and enterprise edge devices, enabling local inference, cutting round‑trip time, and keeping proprietary data off third‑party servers.
  • Autonomous deployment agents monitor CI/CD pipelines, detect performance regressions, isolate faulty micro‑services, patch Kubernetes configurations, and execute zero‑downtime rollouts. Human engineers intervene only for high‑risk architectural changes or policy approvals.
  • Autonomous agents can ingest real‑time shipping telemetry, customs databases, and weather feeds to recalculate optimal routes, renegotiate carrier contracts, and reroute cargo instantly.
  • In finance, agents execute portfolio‑hedging strategies instantly, bypassing human reaction latency during flash crashes or sudden market shifts.

🔒 Security considerations

  • CRITICAL SECURITY WARNING: Autonomous agents with write permissions to production databases or cloud infrastructure are a severe vector for catastrophic failure.
  • Always implement deterministic validation gates and human‑in‑the‑loop checkpoints before executing irreversible write operations, database migrations, or financial transactions that exceed defined thresholds.
  • Restrict agent permissions to scoped, ephemeral tokens with minimal necessary privileges.

💡 Why it matters

  • Shifts AI from reactive text generation to proactive task execution, closing the feedback loop between failure and remediation.
  • Reduces latency, compute cost, and reliance on centralized cloud resources.
  • Enables real‑time adaptation to volatile global trade conditions and fast‑moving financial markets.
  • Allows engineers to focus on strategic decisions rather than routine scripting and debugging.

#AutonomousAI #MultiAgent #EdgeComputing #AIOps

Source: Autonomous AI Trends 2025: Top Tech Drives Next AI Era

item.title: GPS-Bench: An Evidence-Grounded Benchmark for Governance Policy Simulation
item.description:
GPS-Bench: An Evidence-Grounded Benchmark for Governance Policy Simulation

A new benchmark called GPS‑Bench has been introduced to evaluate large‑language‑model (LLM) based policy simulations using public evidence about policies, actors, and outcomes.

🔍 Overview

  • Policy analysis requires more than predicting whether a proposal will pass; it must identify who is affected, how actors respond, and what follows. (“Policy analysis requires…”)
  • Existing LLM‑based simulations model these processes at scale, but their validity is hard to establish without comparing plausible behavior to observed outcomes. (“LLM‑based policy simulations…”)
  • GPS‑Bench provides an evidence‑grounded benchmark that links policies to relevant actors, actor actions, and downstream impacts using legislative records, lobbying disclosures, regulatory documents, corporate filings, economic data and other public evidence. (“We introduce GPS‑Bench…")

🛠️ How it works

  • Actor reconstruction: Actors are rebuilt from the dated record rather than being prompted as archetypes. Each persona is an evidence object with provenance. (“Actors are reconstructed…”)
  • Evaluation sets: A human‑annotated pool forms the Gold evaluation set. Cases labeled by a separate LLM from retrieved evidence serve as Silver supervision and are never used as test labels. (“a human‑annotated pool…”)
  • Unified inference: Every inference mode reads the same grounded state and emits the same schema, enabling a controlled comparison of multi‑agent simulation approaches. (“Because every inference mode…”)

📊 Inference modes compared

Mode Description
Joint reasoning Actors reason together on the shared grounded state
Independent & communicating actor agents Actors act separately but can exchange proposals
Graph‑based methods Uses graph structures to model actor relationships
Weight‑level fine‑tuning Fine‑tunes model weights on the grounded record
(“we contrast joint reasoning, independent and communicating actor agents, graph‑based methods and weight‑level fine‑tuning over one policy state.”)

📈 Findings

  • Fine‑tuning on the grounded record yields the strongest actor‑level impact prediction. (“Fine‑tuning on the grounded record gives the strongest actor‑level impact prediction…")
  • Decomposition does not outperform fine‑tuning, but it adds mechanistic insight. (“…and decomposition does not beat it; what decomposition adds is mechanism.”)
  • Agents hold private, non‑identical evidence, each seeing only its own exposure clause. (“Agents hold private, non‑identical evidence…”)
  • Agents address named partners with concrete joint proposals, specifying what they offer, what they need, and why cooperation beats acting alone; these coalitions can be checked against commitments recorded in the evidence. (“…address named partners with concrete joint proposals…so the coalitions that form can be checked against the commitments the record holds.”)

💡 Why it matters

  • GPS‑Bench creates a common empirical setting for studying when evidence, actor modelling, and multi‑agent interaction improve the prediction and interpretation of policy outcomes. (“GPS‑Bench therefore gives a common empirical setting…")
  • By grounding simulations in public records, the benchmark moves policy‑simulation research toward observable, verifiable behavior rather than purely plausible speculation.

#AI #policySimulation #benchmarks #multiAgent #LLM

Source: GPS-Bench: A Governance Policy Benchmark for Automating Policy Analysis

item.title: NS-Copilot: LLM‑Driven Multi‑Agent System for End‑to‑End Neuroscience Analysis
item.description:
NS-Copilot: LLM‑Driven Multi‑Agent System for End‑to‑End Neuroscience Analysis

A new system called NS‑Copilot has been introduced that uses large language models and a multi‑agent architecture to automate neuroscience data analysis.

🔍 Overview

  • NS‑Copilot is an LLM‑driven multi‑agent system for neuroscience analysis.
  • It autonomously supports end‑to‑end workflows for diverse professional tasks.
  • The system unifies domain‑specific pre‑trained models.
  • It supports key neuroscience modalities, including EEG and extracellular spike data, through a natural‑language interface.

🧩 How it works

  • Given raw data and a task description, NS‑Copilot orchestrates agents with specialized roles:
    • Planning
    • Adaptive control
    • Code generation
    • Result synthesis
  • This orchestration enables analysis without dataset‑specific heuristics.

Supported modalities

Modality Supported
EEG ✅
Extracellular spike data ✅

📊 Evaluation

  • NS‑Copilot was evaluated on neuroscience benchmarks spanning:
    • Alzheimer’s disease
    • Parkinson’s disease
    • Working memory spike decoding
  • Across 8 trials per task, the system consistently outperformed strong baselines on the primary metric.

💡 Why it matters

  • Demonstrates effective and scalable neuroscience analysis using LLM‑driven multi‑agent coordination.
  • Reduces the need for hand‑crafted, dataset‑specific heuristics.
  • Provides a natural‑language interface that can streamline complex analytical pipelines for researchers.

#Neuroscience #LLM #MultiAgent #AI #NS-Copilot

Source: NS-Copilot: An LLM-Driven Agent System for Autonomous Neuroscience Analysis

item.title: SCOPED-Hiring diagnoses fairness in LLM-based hiring multi-agent systems

SCOPED-Hiring diagnoses fairness in LLM-based hiring multi-agent systems

A new process‑aware fairness diagnosis pipeline called SCOPED‑Hiring has been introduced for LLM‑based hiring multi‑agent systems.

🔍 Overview

  • SCOPED‑Hiring is a fairness diagnosis pipeline specifically designed for LLM‑based hiring MAS.
  • It focuses on outcome‑based fairness audits that can miss risks within the decision trajectory.

🧩 How it works

  • Constructs controlled resume variants.
  • Runs role‑based hiring committees.
  • Logs 311K structured decision trajectories.
  • Converts trajectory fields into quantitative fairness signals organized by six diagnostic lenses:
    Lens
    final outcome
    counterfactual
    process
    pathway
    dynamic
    design effects

📊 Findings

  • Balanced final hire rates can mask hidden trajectory unfairness.
  • Specific hidden effects identified:
    • Career gaps trigger suspicion.
    • Proxy cues shape qualification judgments.
    • Identity cues lead to unequal investigation.

🛠️ Repair impact

  • Targeted repair guided by the diagnoses reduces total layered burden by 72.3%.
  • The same repair shifts the overall hire rate by only 1.86 pp.

💡 Why it matters

  • Demonstrates that process diagnosis can guide effective fairness repairs in high‑stakes LLM‑based decision systems.
  • Highlights the need to look beyond final outcomes when auditing multi‑agent AI workflows.

#AIfairness #MultiAgent #HiringAI #ProcessAudit

Source: Beyond Outcome Gaps: Process-Aware Fairness Diagnosis for LLM-based Multi-Agent Decision Systems
